2027-03-29.title: Monday of Hevoro week · Easter Monday
readings: You have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to him who has been raised
The guards are paid to say the body was stolen
2027-03-29.alt: Hevoro week, the first week of the season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection). Hevoro means white: the week is kept as one great day of Easter joy. The fast is over: the whole week is kept as Easter.
2027-03-29.verse: In the same way, my friends, you have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, to him who has been raised from the dead in order that we may bear fruit for God.
theo: Christ is risen! The Church keeps this whole week as one great day of Easter, and on its first weekday she reads what happened in Jerusalem while the women were running to tell the disciples. Two reports leave the same empty tomb. The women carry the truth to the disciples; some of the guard carry it to the chief priests. And there the truth is buried under money: the soldiers are given “a large sum of money” and told, “You must say, ‘His disciples came by night and stole him away while we were asleep.’” St Augustine asked, with a smile, what kind of witnesses these were: if they were asleep, how did they see who took the body? (in substance). Matthew adds that “this story is still told among the Jews to this day,” speaking of an account that circulated in his own time, not passing judgment on a people. The first witnesses of the risen Lord, Mary Magdalene, Peter, John and the apostles, were themselves Jews, and the Church, following the Second Vatican Council (Nostra Aetate 4), never blames the Jewish people for the death of Christ. What the passage shows is something every age knows: the truth of the Resurrection can be paid to be silent, but it cannot be paid to stay dead. The tomb was empty because the very body that was crucified had been raised, glorious and alive (Catechism 640, 645).

St Paul explains what the Resurrection does to us. He uses a picture from marriage: a wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives, but if he dies she is free to belong to another. “In the same way, my friends, you have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, to him who has been raised from the dead in order that we may bear fruit for God.” In Baptism we died with Christ; now we belong to the risen Lord as a bride belongs to her husband. The old life of “sinful passions” bore “fruit for death”; the new life bears fruit for God. “But now we are discharged from the law, dead to that which held us captive, so that we are slaves not under the old written code but in the new life of the Spirit.” Easter is not only a fact about Jesus. It is a new belonging for us: we are his, and he is alive.

How do we keep Hevoro week? Hevoro means white. In the early Church those baptized at Easter wore their white garments through this whole week, and the Church still treats the eight days from Qyomtho to New Sunday as one feast. On Easter night our Church proclaimed the Resurrection and shared the peace of the risen Lord with all the people; this week that joy is carried into ordinary days. Go to the Holy Qurbono on as many days as you can. Greet one another with the Easter greeting: “Christ is risen!” “He is risen indeed!” At home, light the lamp in the evening and sing or say an Easter hymn instead of the Lenten prayers; let the children tell what they saw in church at Easter. Visit or call the sick and the elderly who could not come to the Easter services, and share Easter food with someone who has little. Next Sunday is New Sunday, when the Church hears of the Lord's appearance to Thomas.

2027-03-29.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you are risen from the dead, and no money or lie could keep your tomb closed. Through your Body given for us we have died to the old life, so that we may belong to you. Make our lives bear fruit for God in the new life of the Spirit. Give us courage to tell the truth of your Resurrection, and gladden all who are sad this Easter with the light of your rising. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: The risen body of the Lord, once laid in the tomb, is truly given to us in the Holy Qurbono, so that we may belong to him and bear fruit for God.

quick: The guards were paid to say that the body had been stolen; the tomb was empty because Christ was raised.
Through the body of Christ we died to the old life so that we may belong to the risen Lord.
We serve in the new life of the Spirit and bear fruit for God.
2027-03-29.action: Greet someone today with “Christ is risen!”
2027-03-29.question: To whom do I belong this Easter: to my old habits, or to the risen Lord?

family.explain: On Easter morning the soldiers who guarded Jesus' tomb saw that it was empty. Some leaders paid them money to tell a false story: that Jesus' friends had stolen his body while the soldiers slept. But the truth cannot be hidden. Jesus really rose from the dead, and soon many people saw him alive.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who does not yet know that Jesus is alive.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we tell someone this week that Jesus is risen?”

illus: In a hospital in Thiruvalla a night nurse was told by a senior colleague to change the time written on a chart so that a delay in treatment would not be noticed. The patient had recovered; no one would ever know. It was Easter Monday. She had been to the Easter Qurbono only the night before, and she remembered the soldiers who were paid to change their story. She wrote the true time and reported the delay. She was not thanked for it that week. Some months later the hospital changed its night procedures, and the colleague, to her surprise, came to thank her.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, we rejoice in your Resurrection. Fill this gathering with your Easter joy. Amen.
share: You have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another (Romans 7:4). What does it mean for me to belong to the risen Lord?
Slaves not under the old written code but in the new life of the Spirit (Romans 7:6). What is new in my life this Easter?
So they took the money and did as they were directed (Matthew 28:15). Where am I tempted to keep silent about the truth?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, make us your witnesses.
interc: For the Church throughout the world in this Easter week, that her joy may reach those who are sad.
For all who were baptized or received into full communion this Easter.
For those who are paid or pressured to hide the truth, that they may have courage.
For the sick and elderly who could not come to the Easter services.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, and for friendship between Christians and Jews.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son from the dead, and no power could keep him in the tomb. Make us his own, let our lives bear fruit for you, and send us to tell the truth of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today's Gospel shows two reports leaving the empty tomb. The women run with the truth; some of the guard are paid to say: his disciples came by night and stole him away while we were asleep (Matthew 28:13).

St Augustine asked how sleeping witnesses could know who took the body. The truth of the Resurrection can be paid to be silent, but it cannot be paid to stay dead. The tomb was empty because the body that was crucified had been raised, glorious and alive.

St Paul tells us what this means for us: you have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, to him who has been raised from the dead in order that we may bear fruit for God (Romans 7:4). In Baptism we died with him; now we belong to him.

This is Hevoro week, the white week, kept as one great day of Easter. Let us come to the Holy Qurbono, greet one another with Christ is risen, visit those who could not come to church, and let our lives bear fruit for God. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! On Easter morning some soldiers were paid money to tell a false story about Jesus. But nobody can stop the truth: Jesus really is alive! This whole week is Easter. Can you say to everyone at home today: Christ is risen? And they will answer: He is risen indeed!

sub: Fruit for death, or fruit for God.

q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither.
I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.

concl: The tomb is empty because the crucified body was raised in glory.
In Baptism we died with Christ so that we may belong to him and bear fruit for God.
2027-03-29.resolve: Live this Hevoro week as people who belong to the risen Lord: at his altar, in honest speech, and in works of mercy.
